title: From Your Laptop to the Pipeline: Scaling Custom Agents with GitHub Copilot
talk_summary: A GitHub field engineer tours how Copilot agents are built locally, shared via marketplaces/org repos, and then moved into CI as headless 'agentic workflows' triggered by repo events and gated by human-in-the-loop slash commands. The most transferable ideas are centralizing reusable agent definitions, running agents in the pipeline for observability, and using cost/tool-call telemetry to drive model and prompt optimization.

takeaways.technique: Centralized reusable agent definitions to raise cache hit rate
takeaways.what_they_do: Publishes agents/skills in a central marketplace or org repo so everyone invokes the same standardized agent, arguing exact-match turns on common data raise cache hits and lower the bill.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the cheapest way to use them is to get cash hits... having reusable components will drive up your cash rate

takeaways.technique: Headless one-shot agents in CI triggered by events
takeaways.what_they_do: Runs the CLI in headless mode with a single prompt inside GitHub Actions, triggered on repo events (release, weekly cron) so maintenance agents run on the repo's budget and identity, not a person's laptop.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I can call the Copilot CLI, I can use the dash P command and basically pass it a single prompt one-shot prompt

takeaways.technique: Instrument every agent run and alert on P90 cost
takeaways.what_they_do: Instruments pipeline agents with OpenTelemetry into a logging/SIEM platform, then pivots on average token use and triggers investigation whenever an agent exceeds its expected P90 cost.
takeaways.evidence_quote: every time that an agent exceeds its P90 for what I expect it to cost me to run, go investigate why

takeaways.technique: A/B test front matter and models on failing tool calls
takeaways.what_they_do: When a tool call fails repeatedly, A/B tests different agent front matter or different models to find the cheapest model that still produces correct output.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if I see that a tool call's failing over and over, maybe I want to AB test different front matter or maybe I want to AB test different models

takeaways.what_they_do: Chains pipeline agents (scan → plan → implement → accept) but inserts explicit human approval via an issue slash command before spending money on the next phase.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we'll build in human in the loop triggers for you so that you can review and decide when you're actually going to spend money

takeaways.what_they_do: Runs a scheduled agent that scans the codebase for duplicated code and namespacing problems and files issues rather than fixing directly, keeping human control over what gets fixed.
takeaways.evidence_quote: an agent that looks inside the code base, identifies opportunities for deduplication of code, and then creates a series of issues
